title: documentation-authority-boundary
rawUserRequest: WI-15 documentation-authority-boundary: define canonical, reference, and historical document authority; default agents to current material, require opt-in for reference, exclude archive, and keep one canonical document per topic.
outOfScope: Historical archived Work Items and existing historical documentation records are preserved.
No provider configuration, scheduler, workflow engine, or automatic document migration is introduced.

sources.reason: Defines the required documentation authority model and default reading boundary.
Existing documentation role, canonical-owner, and historical-context model.
Existing machine-readable classification for current and historical documentation context.
Existing front-matter and documentation architecture enforcement point.
Existing agent reading and governed-work rules to align with the default reading boundary.

riskAssessment.reason: A default-reading boundary can accidentally promote historical material or make current documentation undiscoverable; validation and an explicit registry must keep the transition bounded.

reasons: strict pattern .ai/** and scripts/ai_*.py apply to governance and documentation enforcement.

executionDecision.reason: The user supplied the documentation authority policy and authorized governed writes; current documentation metadata and registry provide implementation evidence.

preReviewWarnings: Review that default routing excludes reference and archive material without hiding the explicit opt-in path.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: A machine-readable documentation authority registry defines canonical, reference, and historical records, with one canonical owner per declared topic.
The default agent reading set contains only current canonical instructional documentation; reference requires explicit opt-in and archive is excluded by default.
The validator rejects invalid authority metadata, duplicate canonical ownership, and historical documents presented as current instruction.
The query command is read-only and tests cover default routing, reference opt-in, archive exclusion, and duplicate-canonical rejection.
Documentation and AGENTS rules explain the authority boundary without rewriting historical archives.
guidelines: New public authority-query APIs must be documented and tested.
Default agent reading must not treat reference or historical documentation as current instruction.
Preserve historical documentation and Work Item archives.

intent.problem: Documentation has existing metadata and context records, but agents still lack one bounded machine-readable default reading set that distinguishes current instruction from reference and historical material.
constraints: Use authority values canonical, reference, historical and the requested instructional/status/supersededBy metadata semantics.
Keep docs/reference available only through explicit opt-in and docs/archive excluded by default.
Do not rewrite historical documents or archived Work Items.
Do not add a scheduler, workflow engine, provider configuration, or automatic migration.
intent.rationale: A small registry and validator make authority explicit for agents while preserving existing documentation paths and historical evidence.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Only current canonical instructional documents are returned without opt-in.
Reference documents require opt-in and historical archive documents are never current instruction.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run focused documentation-authority tests with fixture records.

scenarioCoverage.expected: Duplicate canonical ownership for one topic fails validation.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: User explicitly authorized required Contract and governed Work Item writes for this and future Work Items.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff and restore related tests and docs.
